name: Reliable Prompts: Evaluation and Good Practice
summary: The distance between a demo prompt and one that runs in production: measure it, version it and stop trusting luck.
prerequisites: Requires prompt engineering. No programming required, though a little helps with the evaluation harness.
syllabus: The good practices that hold a prompt up in production
Cost and latency in real pipelines

topics.title: Giving few-shot examples to pin down output structure and style
Keeping the prompt short, direct and free of contradictory instructions
Asking for structured output when it makes consumption easier
Using variables and placeholders to reuse the same prompt
Preferring clear instructions to piling up constraints
Controlling the maximum length of the answer
Experimenting with input formats and writing styles
Tuning temperature, top-k and top-p to the task
Delimiting sections with triple backticks or XML markup
Guarding against prompt injection and sanitising user text
Automating evaluation: test sets and unit tests on output
Evaluation metrics: correctness, format, tone and safety
LLM as judge: model-based evaluation and its limits
Versioning prompts and tracking the effect of each change
Documenting decisions, failures and lessons for whoever comes next
Optimising latency and cost in production pipelines
Prompt caching and context reuse
Debiasing: reducing bias introduced by the wording
Prompt ensembling: combining several prompts and voting
LLM self-evaluation
Calibration: aligning stated confidence with actual accuracy
